mechaber.en:
The Laws of Building One Sukkah Under Another Sukkah. Containg 3
paragraphs: Regarding a sukkah that is underneath another sukkah, the top one is valid and the bottom one is invalid. This is so if the bottom one is able to receive pillows and mattresses of the upper one, even with difficulty, and there are ten tefachim between them. However, if there are not ten tefachim between them or there are ten tefachim between them but it is impossible for [the floor of] the upper [sukkah to support a person together with his] pillows and mattresses even with difficulty, the bottom one is valid if it is covered per the law, even if the upper sukkah is' higher than twenty tefachim. If it is not covered per the halachah and valid due to the s'chach of the upper one, the s'chach of that upper sukkah cannot be higher than twenty amot off the ground.

או אפילו ראוי לדיורין מה דתנא חד סק קומי ר' זעירא ואפילו התחתונ' כשרה לית בר נש אמר אפילו אלא דהוא מודה על קדמייתא הדא אמרה דיורין ממש עד כאן לשונו. ופירש הק"ע דאם אין ראוי לדיורין היאך העליונה כשרה ע"ש. וק"ל מה ראיה הרי קיי"ל בסמך הסכך ע"ג אילן אין עולין לה ביו"ט דהוי משתמש באילן ומ"מ אם עבר ועלה יצא י"ח כמ"ש בעטרת זקנים שם בסי' זה ורבי יהודה לשיטתו דסבירא ליה בעשאה ע"ג גמל דפסולה דאינה ראויה לשבעה דבתר דרבנן אזלינן ואם כן הכא נמי נימא דכוונת רבי יהודה הוי באינה ראויה לדיורין אז כשרה התחתונה. ומה דמשמע דאפילו עליונה כשרה יש לו' דמשכחת לה דאינה ראויה לדיורין כגון דסכך התחתונה נסמך ע"ג אילן chokhmat_shlomo.en: Se'if 1 A sukkah beneath an upper sukkah: the upper one is valid and the lower one is invalid, etc. Note: The source of this law is in the first chapter of Sukkah, in the Mishnah. We read in the Yerushalmi, first chapter, halacha 3: Rabbi Yehudah says, if there are no residents in the upper one, the lower one is valid. Does residents mean actual residents, or even fit for residents? One Tanna recited before Rabbi Zeira: and even the lower one is valid. No person says even unless he agrees about the first case. This teaches that it means actual residents. This is the Yerushalmi's wording. The Korban HaEdah explained that if the upper one is not fit for dwelling, how is the upper one valid? See there. This is difficult for me. What proof is there? We rule that if one supported the s'chach on a tree, one may not ascend to it on Yom Tov because he is using the tree, and nevertheless if he transgressed and ascended, he fulfilled his obligation, as written in the Ateret Zekenim here in this siman. Rabbi Yehudah follows his own view, for he holds that if one made it on top of a camel it is invalid because it is not fit for seven days; he follows the rabbinic restriction. If so, here too let us say that Rabbi Yehudah's intent is that when it is not fit for dwelling, the lower one is valid. And what is implied, that even the upper one is valid, can be found in a case where it is not fit for dwelling, such as where the s'chach of the lower sukkah is supported on a tree and is the floor of the upper one. If so, on Shabbos it is not fit for the upper one's dwelling, since one may not ascend to it on Yom Tov or Shabbos. Therefore the lower one is valid, for rabbinically the upper one is not fit for dwelling. Nevertheless, it is still possible to say that the upper one too is valid, for if he transgressed and ascended he fulfilled his obligation. Therefore the word even is used properly. What proof is there? This requires great examination. I have another difficulty: what proof is there? We rule that a sukkah invalid because of make it, and not from what was already made, such as one who hollows out a stack to make a sukkah, is invalid; and likewise with one who placed s'chach over a roof and removed that roof, as the Magen Avraham writes in siman 626. But s'chach higher than twenty is not considered make it and not from what was already made, as the poskim write. Necessarily the reason for the distinction is that where it was not called s'chach at all, such as hollowing out a stack, it is considered make it and not from what was already made. But if it was called s'chach, make it and not from what was already made does not apply, since it was called s'chach from the start, and also the invalidity is not in the s'chach itself but because of another factor, excluding s'chach made of attached material, etc. If so, let us say that Rabbi Yehudah's intent is as follows: certainly as long as both layers of s'chach remain, one can say it is invalid even if there are residents in the upper one, because in the end there are two layers of s'chach. Rabbi Yehudah speaks where the upper one is removed. Then, if there are no residents in the upper one, the lower layer had the name of s'chach upon it, and therefore, although there had been two layers of s'chach, if the upper one is removed the lower one is valid, with no concern of make it and not from what was already made. But if there are residents in the upper one, the lower one is like one who placed s'chach under a roof, like one who hollows out a stack, and like one who placed s'chach inside a house; therefore even if the upper one is removed, the lower one is invalid because of make it and not from what was already made. According to this, if this is the intent, one can still say that Rabbi Yehudah refers to not fit for dwelling. And when he says even the lower one, it means not only that if the lower one were removed it would certainly be permitted to sit below in the lower area by means of the upper s'chach, and this would not be considered make it and not from what was already made, but even in the reverse case, where the upper one was removed and the lower one remained, it too is valid and has no concern of make it and not from what was already made. What proof is this? This requires examination according to the view of Mahari Weil cited by the Magen Avraham in siman 627. But according to the Rema's view it works well, for necessarily Rabbi Yehudah speaks where the upper one is not removed; if it were removed, then even where there are residents in the upper one, the lower one would be valid, no worse than one who placed s'chach under a roof. Consider this carefully. I returned and saw that the same difficulty applies to our Talmud as well, on page 10, where it says: what is not fit for dwelling, etc. Why not say that it speaks where he made it on top of a tree and the like, so that it is not fit for dwelling, and Rabbi Yehudah follows his view while the first Tanna follows his view, for the first Tanna follows the Torah-level status? The second question is likewise difficult; consider it. Now Tosafot's view too is that what is above twenty is not called invalid s'chach. But Rashi's view is that it is invalid s'chach so as to invalidate what is below it opposite it. In my humble opinion there is no dispute here. Rabbeinu Tam proved his view from Eruvin, where part of the s'chach is within twenty, etc. It appears to me to reconcile Rashi's text and view, and to reconcile the sugyot so they do not contradict one another. The reason that what is above twenty does not invalidate what is opposite it and is not called invalid s'chach is because he has the ability to reduce it and lower it, and it itself would become valid. We rule in Kiddushin that anything in one's power is not considered lacking time. It is not comparable to attached material, even though he also has power to cut it, because one can say this resembles what the Talmud answers in Kiddushin chapter 3 regarding one who says to his maidservant, etc.: there, at first she was like an animal, and now another person's consent transfers her. This proves that where there is a change in the body of the thing, the fact that it is in his power does not help. So too here: with attached material, if he detaches it, there will be a change in its body, for at first it was attached and now it is detached, so being in his power does not help. But with s'chach higher than twenty, if he lowers it there is no change in its body, so the fact that he can reduce it helps. This is fine on a weekday, but on Yom Tov he cannot lower it, for that would be dismantling an ohel. See Tosafot in the third chapter of Sukkah, page 33, s.v. niktam me'erev Yom Tov, where it is proven that the Talmud holds that anything requiring a prohibited act is not considered in one's power. If so, since on Shabbos and Yom Tov it is forbidden to reduce it because it is dismantling an ohel, it should invalidate what is below it opposite it. One can say that in truth on Shabbos and Yom Tov it is invalid, and it is valid only for the other days of the festival. But one can ask: it is not a sukkah fit for seven days, since on Shabbos it becomes invalid because of invalid s'chach. Yet according to us, we rule like the Sages, that if one made it on top of an animal it is valid and is not considered a sukkah unfit for seven days, because by Torah law it is fit. If so, here too dismantling a temporary ohel on Shabbos and Yom Tov is only rabbinic; by Torah law it is in his power to reduce it even on Shabbos and Yom Tov, and only rabbinically it is not fit, so it is still fit for seven days. But this is only according to the Sages. According to Rabbi Yehudah there, who holds it is invalid because we follow the rabbinic status, here too it is invalid because it is not fit for seven days. Therefore it works well: in Eruvin the Talmud proceeds according to the halacha, for we rule like the Sages, and therefore what is higher than twenty is not invalid s'chach to invalidate what is opposite it. But here one can say either that Rabbi Yirmeyah holds like Rabbi Yehudah, who follows the rabbinic status, or that he did not want to enter a dispute, and therefore he chose a case where the upper one stands within twenty, in which case it is valid according to everyone. But if it were higher than twenty, it would be invalid according to Rabbi Yehudah, and he does not speak in a disputed case. Therefore Rashi explained as he did. If so, in practical law Rashi too agrees with Rabbeinu Tam, except that on Yom Tov and Shabbos it is invalid. Consider this carefully.

And to magnify the difficulty: when the upper has more shade, the lower also has more shade in a tree such as this — there is no opinion it is valid. And the upper is invalid if it cannot receive pillows through constraint, and Maharshal z"l chapter 5 halakhah 22 erases Machatzit HaShekel and Elkabetz there that one does not fulfill in the upper — a light person on his feet etc. — the lower is invalid, and it is a great stretch to say one estimates each person as he is, and a person who cannot sit in the upper fulfills in the lower — still requires study.

rabbi_akiva_eiger.he: <small>שם </small>לא מקרי סכך פסול. ומ"מ אין ללמוד מכאן דאם העליונה אינה עשויי' לצל בענין דפסול משום תולמ"ה דג"כ כשירה כיון דהסכך בעצמותו אינה פסול ע' סוכה דף י"ז ע"א דע"כ מוכח דפסולה דתולמ"ה גרע טפי מפסול למעלה מכ' דהרי לקמן סי' תרל"ה ס"ה פסקי' דאם מה שמחוץ להכשר סוכה הוא למעלה מכ' כשר מדין פסל היוצא מן הסוכה כיון דאין בעצמותו סכך פסול. ואלו לקמן סי' תרל"ה גבי חוטט בגדיש פסקי' דאם מה שהוא חוץ להכשר סוכה יש בו משום תולמ"ה פסול לישב בו ע"ש כנלע"ד בעזה"י:
rabbi_akiva_eiger.en: <small>There</small> It is not called invalid s'chach. Nevertheless, one should not learn from here that if the upper one was not made for shade, so that it is invalid because of make it, and not from what was already made, it would also be valid because the s'chach itself is not inherently invalid. See Sukkah 17a, where it is necessarily proven that it is invalid, for the invalidity of make it and not from what was already made is worse than the invalidity of being higher than twenty. Below in siman 635:5 we rule that if the part outside the valid sukkah area is higher than twenty, it is valid by the law of the extension that emerges from the sukkah, since it is not inherently invalid s'chach. But below in siman 635 regarding one who hollows out a stack, we rule that if the part outside the valid sukkah area has the invalidity of make it and not from what was already made, it is forbidden to sit there; see there. So it appears to me, with God's help.

turei_zahav.he: אפי' אם העליונה כו'. משמע אע"פ שהעליונ' ג"כ צלתה מרובה מחמת'. ואע"ג דבסי' תרכ"ז פסל לכ"ע אם הסכך פסול דהיינו האילן היא צלתה מרובה מחמת' שאני הכא דהעליון אינו נקרא סכך פסול כיון שאין הפסול מחמת עצמו רק מחמת שיעור הגובה זו היא סברת ר"ת בתו':
turei_zahav.en: Even if the upper one, etc. This implies even though the upper one also has more shade than sun. Although in siman 627 everyone invalidates if the invalid s'chach, namely the tree, has more shade than sun, here is different, for the upper s'chach is not called invalid s'chach, since its invalidity is not intrinsic but only because of the measure of height. This is Rabbeinu Tam's reasoning in Tosafot.

yad_ephraim.he: (ס״ק ו׳) ואפשר בזה״ז שאין רגילות כו, דאף אם יניח לא מיקרי משתמש במחובר כמ״ש סי׳ של״ו אינו מובן שהרי הרא״ש אוסר מהאי טעמא דשמא יניח אם כי ע״כ ס״ל דמיקרי משתמש בתחוב׳ לי׳ והיה לו לומר דלא גזרי׳ שמא יניח כיון דבזה״ז אין רגילין להניח ולא גזרי׳ בכה״ג ומרא׳ בכוונת דבריו עפ״י מ״ש בסי׳ של״ו שדעת הרא״ש באם נוטלין מן האילן לא מקרי משתמש במחובר רק הטעם דאסור להניח נר על האילן ביו״ט שמא יעלה על האילן כדי ליטלו והק׳ ע״ז מדברי הרא״ש שבכאן דס״ל דאסור ליטול חפץ מעל האילן כו׳ ולכאורה אינו מובן דדלמא גם בזה האיסור שמא יעלה על האילן צ״ל דהתם א״ש דאסור להניח על האילן שמא יעלה עליו ליטלו וחדא גזירה הוא משא״כ כאן אם באנו לאסור משום שמא יעלה כו׳ הו״ל גזירה לגזירה דהא באמת אינו מניח רק דנגזור שמא מניח ושמא יעלה הו״ל גזרה לגזרה ומזה מוכיח דאף אי לא גזרינן שמא יעלה אסור להניח משום משתמש במחובר והכיח בקושיא ודעת ה״ה באמת הוא כן דאסור משום משתמש במחובר וכדי שלא יקשה עליו ממ״ש הרא״ש להוכיח מהא דקושרין חבל בפרה כ׳ המג״א לחלק דדוקא אילן שדרך תשמישו ליטול ממנו ולהניח ע״ג אבל בהמה אין דרך תשמישו בזה ע״ש ולפי״ז גם לפי ההוכח׳ שמוכיח המג״א מהרא״ש דכאן דליטול ממנו הוי משתמש במחובר ג״כ צריך לחלק בין אילן שדרך תשמישו כו' ובין בהמה דאל״כ מקשי על הרא״ש דכאן מהא דקושרין חבל בפרה וע״כ לחלק דאילן דרך תשמישו הו״ל משתמש במחובר והנה בלשון הרא״ש שכ׳ גזירה שמא ינוח חפצו על הסכך מ״ל דלאו ברגילות תליא מילתא רק דגזור שמא כשנתת לו לעלות אם יארע שיצטרך להניח חפצו ויניח יהיה משתמש במחובר אך בלשון ה״ה מבואר שהיו רגילים להניח ואם כן י״ל אם כוונת הרא״ש כן דגזרה שמא יניח כו׳ משום שהוא רגיל כן אבל אם אינו רגילות מה״ת לחוש לזה ולפי״ז נראה דאתי שפיר דברי המג"א וחסר בדבריו מלת ועוד וכצ"ל ואפשר בזה"ז כו' ולא גזרינן שמא יניח על הסבך ועוד דאף אם יניח כו' וכוונת דבריו דמתחלה מייתי דברי הרא"ש ויש לפרש דלאו ברגילות תליא אלא גזרה הוא שמא יארע כן וקצת קשה לומר כן דמה"ת נמציא גזרה בזה שיעשה כן דהא קמן שאין רגילות לעשות כן ואין לגזור בשביל איזה מאורע דלא שכיח ולזה מייתי דברי ה"ה שכ' שהרי רגילים כו' וכיון דבזמנם היו רגילים בזה שפיר גזרו שלא לעלות שמא יעשה כרגילות להניח שם כו' וע"ז כ' וכיון שהעיקר האיסור מחמת שמא יעשה כרגילות ממילא דבזה"ז שאין אנו רגילין שרי ולא גזרינן שמא יניח על הסכך (ומ"ש המג"א לא אסר משום דבר שבמנין כו' סי' קי"ז הוא כמו מאמר מוסגר מוקף בין שני חצאי עיגול כאשר נמצא בדברי המג"א כמה פעמים) ושוב כ' ועוד דאף אם יניח לא מיקרי מסתמא במחובר כמ"ש סימן של"ו ר"ל דשם מבואר מההיא דקשירת חבל בפר' שמותר מוכרח לחלק דלא מיקרי הנחה משתמש במחובר אא"כ דדרך תשמישו בכך ליטול ממנו ולהניח על גבו וכיון דבזה"ז אין רגילין להשתמש בזה דמי לקשירת חבל בפרה שמותר וכיון דמחמת משתמש במחובר אין חשש אין לחוש לשמא יעלה באילן דמה"ט אסור להניח נר על האילן ביו"ט דהתם שייך גזרה שמא יעלה כיון שהניח הנר משא"כ כאן שבאמת אינו מניח רק שיגזור שמא יניח ושמא יעלה הו"ל גזרה לגזרה וכמש"ל בדברי המג"א סימן של"ו והיינו דדייק המ"א בלישנ' וכת' דאף אם יניח לא מיקרי משתמש במחובר ולא קאמר דאין לגזור שמא יניח דמותר להניח אך כוונתו כמ"ש דלהניח באמת ודאי אסור אף דליכא משום דמשתמש במחובר מכל מקום אסור להניח משום גזירה שמא יעלה באילן ולכך כתב דעכ"פ לא מיקרי משתמש במחובר שאם היה אסור משום משתמש חדא גזירה היא וכיון שמחמת זה אין איסור שוב בכאן שבאמת אינו מניח מותר ליכנס לסוכה דנגזר שמא יניח ושמא יעלה היא גזרה כן נלענ"ד נכון ובאמת אף לא (נגיה) בדברי המג"א מלת ועוד גם כן יש לכוון דברי המג"א עפ"י מ"ש אך יותר קרוב להוסיף מלת ועוד שבזה יבואו הדברים מתוקנים היטב ונכון בעזה"י:
yad_ephraim.en: (Se'if katan 6) And perhaps nowadays, when it is not customary, etc.; for even if he places it there, it is not called using attached material, as written in siman 336. This is not understood, for the Rosh forbids for this very reason, lest he place something there, and he must necessarily hold that it is called using what is attached. The Magen Avraham should have said that we do not decree lest he place something there, since nowadays it is not customary to place things there, and in such a case we do not decree. The intent of his words appears according to what he wrote in siman 336, that according to the Rosh, if one removes something from a tree it is not called using attached material. Rather, the reason it is forbidden to place a candle on a tree on Yom Tov is lest he ascend the tree to take it. The Magen Avraham challenged this from the Rosh's words here, where he holds that it is forbidden to take an object from atop the tree, etc. At first glance this is not understood, for perhaps here too the prohibition is lest he ascend the tree. One must say that there it works well: it is forbidden to place something on the tree lest he ascend it to remove it, and that is one decree. But here, if we came to forbid because perhaps he will ascend, it would be a decree upon a decree, for in truth he is not placing anything there; we would have to decree lest he place something, and lest he ascend. That would be a decree upon a decree. From this the Magen Avraham proves that even if we do not decree lest he ascend, placing it there is forbidden because it is use of attached material, and he proves it by way of difficulty. The view of the Maggid Mishneh is indeed that it is forbidden because of using attached material. In order to avoid difficulty from what the Rosh wrote to prove from the law that one may tie a rope to a cow, the Magen Avraham wrote a distinction: specifically a tree, whose normal use is to take from it and place on it, is considered use in this manner; but an animal is not normally used in this way. See there. According to this, even according to the proof that the Magen Avraham derives from the Rosh here, that taking from it is considered using attached material, one must still distinguish between a tree, whose normal use, etc., and an animal. Otherwise one could challenge the Rosh here from the law that one may tie a rope to a cow. Necessarily one must distinguish that with a tree, since this is its manner of use, it is called using attached material. Now in the Rosh's wording, that he wrote a decree lest he place his object on the s'chach, perhaps the matter does not depend on regular practice. Rather, they decreed that once you allow him to ascend, if it should happen that he needs to place his object down and he places it there, he will be using attached material. However, in the Maggid Mishneh's wording it is explicit that they were accustomed to place items there. If so, one can say that if the Rosh's intent is that it is a decree lest he place, etc., it is because that was the regular practice; but if it is not the practice, why should we be concerned for this? According to this, the Magen Avraham's words are well understood, though the word moreover is missing. The text should read: and perhaps nowadays, etc., and we do not decree lest he place something on the s'chach; moreover, even if he does place, etc. His intent is that he first brings the Rosh's words, which could be explained as not depending on regular practice but as a decree lest such a case occur. Yet it is somewhat difficult to say so, for why should we invent a decree that he will do this, when we see that it is not customary to do so? We do not decree because of an uncommon possibility. Therefore he brings the Maggid Mishneh's words, that they were accustomed, etc. Since in their times they were accustomed to this, it is understandable that they decreed not to ascend lest he act as usual and place something there. On this he wrote: since the core prohibition is because he may act as usual, it follows that nowadays, when we are not accustomed to this, it is permitted, and we do not decree lest he place something on the s'chach. What the Magen Avraham wrote, that it is not forbidden because of something enacted by a formal count, etc., in siman 117, is like a parenthetical remark, as is found many times in the Magen Avraham. Then he wrote further: moreover, even if he places something there, it is presumably not called using attached material, as written in siman 336. That means that there, from the case of tying a rope to a cow, where it is permitted, it is necessary to distinguish: placing something is not called using attached material unless it is the normal way of using it, to take from it and place upon it. Since nowadays people are not accustomed to use the s'chach that way, it is like tying a rope to a cow, which is permitted. And since there is no concern of using attached material, there is no concern lest he ascend the tree, for that is the reason it is forbidden to place a candle on a tree on Yom Tov. There, the decree lest he ascend applies because he actually placed the candle there. But here, where in truth he is not placing anything, to decree lest he place and lest he ascend would be a decree upon a decree, as I wrote above regarding the Magen Avraham's words in siman 336. This is why the Magen Avraham was precise in his wording and wrote that even if he places it there, it is not called using attached material; he did not say that one should not decree lest he place, because it is permitted to place. His intent is as I wrote: in truth, placing is certainly forbidden, for even if there is no issue of using attached material, it is still forbidden to place it there because of a decree lest he ascend the tree. Therefore he wrote only that in any event it is not called using attached material. If it were forbidden because of use, it would be one decree. But since there is no prohibition on that account, here, where he is not actually placing anything, it is permitted to enter the sukkah, for decreeing lest he place and lest he ascend would be a decree upon a decree. So it appears to me to be correct. In truth, even without emending the Magen Avraham's words by adding moreover, his words can be aligned according to what I wrote; but it is closer to add the word moreover, for with this the words are properly arranged and correct, with God's help.

mechaber.he: עשאה בראש הגמל או בראש האילן כשרה ואין עולין לה בי"ט מקצתה על האילן ומקצתה בדבר אחר אם הוא בענין שאם ינטל האילן תשאר היא עומדת ולא תפול עולין לה ביום טוב ואם לאו אין עולין לה ביום טוב:
mechaber.en: [If a person] constructs his sukkah on a camel or on top of a tree, i.e., the treetop, it is valid. One may not, however, climb up to it on a festival, even a little bit on the tree and a little bit on something else, if [the sukkah] is constructed in such a manner that if the tree was removed, it would still stand on the other support without falling on Yom Tov. And if not, he may not climb up on it on Yom Tov.

ateret_zekenim.he: כשרה ואין עולין לה בי"ט וה"ה אם עבר ועלה בי"ט יצא ידי חובתו:
ateret_zekenim.en: When he and she do not believe in the High Court and the the Omnipresent, if he has passed away, he will be his duty:

baer_heitev.he:
האילן. היינו כשהסכך יוכל לעמוד בלא אילן שסמכו על קונדסין דאל"כ אסור דגזרינן שמא יסכך בו כמ"ש סי' תרכ"ט סעיף ז'. ר"ן מ"א:
עולין. ואם עבר ועלה יצא י"ח ואם הסוכה על הארץ והקנים של הסכך נסמכים על האילן שרי ולא גזרינן שמא יניח על הסכך. מ"א ע"ש:
baer_heitev.en:
The tree. This is where the s'chach can stand without the tree, because he supported it on poles. Otherwise it is forbidden, for we decree lest he use the tree itself as s'chach, as written in siman 629:7. Ran; Magen Avraham.
One may ascend. If he transgressed and ascended, he fulfilled his obligation. If the sukkah is on the ground and the reeds of the s'chach are supported by the tree, it is permitted, and we do not decree lest he place something upon the s'chach. See the Magen Avraham there.

beer_hagolah.he:
משנה שם
דאסור להשתמש ביום טוב בבעלי חיים במחובר
beer_hagolah.en:
(א) Change there

(ב) Do not use a good day for animals in the organ

eliyah_rabbah.he: [ג] ביום טוב אין עולין וכו'. ואם עבר ועלה יצא ידי חובת סוכה:
eliyah_rabbah.en: On a good day, there is no spice and so on. If it is past and past, it is the duty of the the Omnipresent:

machatzit_hashekel.he: (ס"ק ג) למעל' מכ'. גם הוא מצויין בטעות בדפוס וקאי על הרישא דמכשיר אפי' למעלה מכ' כיון שהתחתונ' לבד' בלי צירוף העליונ' הוא צלתה מ"מ. עז"כ מ"א ולא אמרינן מה שכנגד סכך הפסול כו' והיינו אפילו לדעת י"א הראשון בסי' תרפ"ו דהא מיירי כאן שסכך העליון היא צלתה מ"מ אפ"ה כשרה דסכך העליון מצד עצמו כשר אלא שהמקום גורם לפוסלו:
machatzit_hashekel.en: (Se'if katan 3) Higher than twenty. This too is marked incorrectly in the printing, and refers to the first clause, which validates even when it is higher than twenty, since the lower sukkah by itself, without joining the upper one, has more shade than sun. On this the Magen Avraham wrote: and we do not say that what is opposite the invalid s'chach, etc. This is even according to the first some say opinion in siman 626, for here we speak where the upper s'chach has more shade than sun, and nevertheless it is valid, because the upper s'chach in itself is valid; only its location causes it to be invalid.

magen_avraham.he:
האילן כשרה. היינו כשהסכך יכול לעמוד בלא אילן שסמכו על קונדסין דאל"כ אסור דגזרינן שמא יסכך בו כמ"ש סי' תרכ"ט ס"ז [ר"ן]:
ואין עולין לה. אפי' הסוכה על הארץ והקני' של הסכך נסמכים על האילן אסור גזירה שמא יניח חפציו על הסכך [רא"ש ורי"ו] ומ"מ פ"ד כ' וז"ל שהיו רגילים להניח ולתלות בסכך חפציהם ולהשתמש בהם עכ"ל ואפשר בזמן הזה שאין רגילות להשתמש שם שרי ולא אסור משום דבר שבמנין כיון שאינו אלא משום חששא כמ"ש בי"ד סי' קי"ו ולא גזרי' שמא יניח על הסכך דאף אם יניח לא מקרי משתמש במחובר כמ"ש סי' של"ו ס"א:
magen_avraham.en:
The tree, it is valid. This is where the s'chach can stand without the tree, because he supported it on poles. Otherwise it is forbidden, for we decree lest he use the tree as s'chach, as written in siman 629:7, in the name of the Ran.
And one may not ascend to it. Even if the sukkah is on the ground and the reeds of the s'chach are supported by the tree, it is forbidden, as a decree lest he place his objects on the s'chach, as the Rosh and Rabbeinu Yerucham write. Nevertheless, the Perishah wrote: they were accustomed to place and hang their objects on the s'chach and use them. Perhaps nowadays, when it is not customary to use it that way, it is permitted. It is not forbidden as a decree that required a formal count, since it is only because of a concern, as written in Yoreh De'ah 116. We also do not decree lest he place something on the s'chach, for even if he does place it there, it is not called using attached material, as written in siman 336:1.

mishnah_berurah.he:
(טו) בראש הגמל - היינו שעשה שם הדפנות בין חטוטרותיה וסיכך על גבן:
(טז) בראש האילן - תיקן מושבו בראשו ועשה שם מחיצות וסכך:
(יז) ואין עולין לה - מפני שאסור להשתמש ביו"ט בבע"ח ובמחובר כמ"ש ריש סימן של"ו. ואפילו אם הסוכה היא על הארץ אלא שהקנים של הסכך מסומכין על האילן אסור לעלות לה בשבת ויו"ט גזירה שמא ישתמש בהסכך שיניח שם חפציו או יתלה בו שום דבר ונמצא משתמש על ידי האילן ואפשר דדוקא בימים הראשונים שהיו רגילין להשתמש בסכך להניח ולתלות שם חפציהם אבל עכשיו שאין רגילין בכך אין חוששין לכך ומותר לעלות לתוכה אף בשבת ויו"ט ומ"מ לכתחלה אין לסמוך את הסכך על האילן שאין מעמידין את הסכך לכתחלה אלא בדבר הראוי לסיכוך כמ"ש בסימן תרכ"ט ע"ש הטעם. ואם נעץ קונדסין באילן וסמך הסכך עליהן שרי אף לכתחלה:
(יח) ביו"ט - ואם עבר ועלה ביו"ט יצא ידי חובתו ועיין בפמ"ג שמסופק אם אין לו ביו"ט רק סוכה ע"ג בהמה או אילן אם מותר לו לכתחלה לעלות ע"ש ובבכורי יעקב מסיק דאסור דחכמים פטרוהו ע"ש:
(יט) מקצתה על האילן ומקצתה בדבר אחר - היינו שעשה מקצת קרקעית סוכתו ומקצת דפנותיה על ראש האילן ומקצת קרקעיתה ומקצת דפנותיה על דבר אחר וסיכך על הדפנות אם היא עשויה בענין שאם ינטל האילן תשאר היא עומדת על הדבר אחר ולא תפול וכו':
(כ) עולין לה ביו"ט - היינו בסולם שלא על דרך האילן:
(כא) אין עולין לה ביו"ט - דכיון שסמיכתה על האילן נמצא כשנכנס לתוכה משתמש באילן:

(15) At the top of the camel - This means that he made the walls there between its humps and placed s'chach over them.
(16) At the top of the tree - He prepared his seat at the top of it and made partitions and s'chach there.
(17) And one may not ascend to it - Because it is forbidden on Yom Tov to use a living creature or attached vegetation, as written at the beginning of siman 336. Even if the sukkah is on the ground, but the reeds of the s'chach are supported by the tree, it is forbidden to ascend to it on Shabbos and Yom Tov, as a decree lest he use the s'chach by placing his objects there or hanging something on it, and thus be using the tree indirectly. Perhaps this applies specifically in earlier times, when people were accustomed to use the s'chach to place and hang their objects there. But now that people are not accustomed to do so, we are not concerned for this, and it is permitted to enter it even on Shabbos and Yom Tov. Nevertheless, initially one may not support the s'chach on the tree, for initially the s'chach may be supported only with something fit for s'chach, as written in siman 629; see there for the reason. If he inserted poles into the tree and supported the s'chach on them, it is permitted even initially.
(18) On Yom Tov - If he transgressed and ascended on Yom Tov, he fulfilled his obligation. See the Peri Megadim, who is uncertain whether, if on Yom Tov he has only a sukkah on top of an animal or a tree, he may initially ascend to it; see there. The Bikkurei Yaakov concludes that it is forbidden, for the Sages exempted him; see there.
(19) Part of it on the tree and part of it on another item - This means that he made part of the floor of his sukkah and part of its walls on top of the tree, and part of its floor and part of its walls on another item, and placed s'chach over the walls, if it is made in such a way that if the tree were removed it would remain standing on the other item and not fall, etc.
(20) One may ascend to it on Yom Tov - This means by a ladder, not by way of the tree.
(21) One may not ascend to it on Yom Tov - Since its support is on the tree, when he enters it he is using the tree.

peri_megadim.he: אין עט״ז עא״ר ג׳ אם עבר ועלה יי״ח וי״ל הא הוי מה״ב כיון דא״א אם לא בעבירה עתוס׳ ריש לולב הגזול ואף בדרבנן מה״ב א״י י״ח ולכתחלה נמי בליל א׳ מ״ע שאוכל כזית פת שם לא אתי עשה ודחי לדרבנן כשופר בסימן תקפ״א סכ״א וכ״ב וצ״ע. עיין בגמרא כ״ג א׳ לר״י חג הסוכות שבעת ימים הראויה לז׳ ומכל מקום מ״ה חזיא משמע לכ״ע דרשא גמורא היא ובדף כ״ז ב׳ עשה סוכה בחג לרבנן דר״א מ״מ סוכה הראויה לז׳ נמי הוי דרשינן אלא שלא יצויר ואי בנה סוכה ברשות הרבים ע״ג בהמה ובשבת שביתת בהמתו ד״ת עכ״פ זה בהולכת ד״א ברה״ר או מרה״י לרה״י דלא עדיפא מאדם כמבואר וראיתי בתה״ד סוכה הראויה לז׳ ושבת בתוך ז׳ צ״ע דבלא״ה בי״ט א׳ אסור כפירש״י ז״ל ואולי למ״ש בסי׳ תקי״ד דביתו נשרף ואין לו מקום לאכול מותר לכבות דהוי אוכל נפש י״ל ה״ה דל״ג לעלות באילן ובהמה כה״ג ביו״ט דאוכל נפש שרי רחמנא מש״ה פי׳ דשבת תמיד בתוך שבעה לא ראויה לז׳ אי לאו דמ״ה שרי. וצ״ע לדידן באין לו סוכה אחרת כ״א באילן או ע״ג בהמה אי עולין בי״ט דהוי כאוכל נפש ומיהו שנשרף. ועפ״י בחידושיו במ״ש אין עולין בי״ט עב״י א״ח תקי״ד לר״י מכשירין וכאן לר״י הוא וא״ש בתה״ד ולרש״י י״ל ואפשר לעשות מעי״ט ועיין ביצה בזה. ורש״י כ״ב ב׳ דעבר ועלה יי״ח עמ״ש:
peri_megadim.en: There is no Taz — Rosh chapter 3: if one transgressed and went up and fulfilled — some say this is mitzvah through transgression since it is impossible except through transgression; Tosafot beginning of Lulav stolen, and even for rabbinic mitzvah through transgression one does not fulfill; and l'chatchila also on the first night there is a positive commandment that one eats an olive-size of bread there — the positive commandment does not come and override rabbinic, as shofar in siman 681 seif 21 and 22 — requires study. See Gemara 23a for R' Yehuda: the festival of Sukkot seven days — fit for seven; nevertheless Mishnah implies for all it is a full derashah; and 27b positive commandment to make sukkah on the festival — for Rabbanan of R' Eliezer, nevertheless a sukkah fit for seven is also expounded, only it should not be conceived; and if one built sukkah in public domain on an animal and on Shabbat its rest is biblical — in any case this is carrying, whether public domain to private or private to private, not better than a person as explained. I saw in Teshuvot Divrei Chamudot: sukkah fit for seven and Shabbat within seven — requires study, for otherwise on the first day forbidden as Rashi explained; perhaps for what is written in siman 514 that his house burned and he has nowhere to eat — permitted to extinguish as life-threatening — one could say similarly no prohibition to climb a tree and animal such on Yom Tov as life-threatening the Merciful One permitted; therefore he explained Shabbat always within seven is not fit for seven unless for what is permitted. Requires study for us: if he has no other sukkah except in a tree or on an animal, whether they climb on Yom Tov as life-threatening; however it burned. And according to his innovations in what he wrote one does not climb on Yom Tov — Bach 514 for R' Yehuda validates, and here for R' Yehuda it is, and Bach in Teshuvot Divrei Chamudot, and for Rashi one could say, and perhaps to make from egg — see Beitzah on this. Rashi 22b one who transgressed and went up fulfilled — see his words.
